proposal:
AUDIT (code read, nothing executed). compression._verify_certificate builds blocks from every dense original clause, confines each block's forms to its support, compares block and quotient clauses on all 2^w local points and checks P*L=I entrywise. Conjunction over blocks plus linear surjectivity gives SAT(F) iff SAT(Q). probe() can only delete input clauses, and only an UNSAT 2-SAT quotient decides. I find no soundness defect. Work: step runs at most 1+2*sum_layers|states| times. Each call is polynomial under the caps except the rank-deficient branch of dual_certificate (unmodular HNF on up to 128 rows, no stated bit bound). So 'total work <= poly * sum of layer sizes' is one HNF lemma short of proved. Unimplemented saving: run elim_plus before refute and skip refute when DP is decisive; status and peak cannot change.

MECHANISM UD (certified un-distribution). For clause sets A_1..A_k let PROD be all unions a_1 u ... u a_k. A certificate is (A_1..A_k, M) where every non-tautological member of PROD lies in F or in the listed deficit M.
Lemma UD (distributivity). models(F) = union_i models(F + A_i) u union_{m in M} models(F restricted by not-m). Proof: if a model of F falsifies some a_i in every A_i, their union is false, hence not in F, hence in M, and the model satisfies not-m. Each child implies F.
Check: enumerate |PROD| <= |F|+|M| unions against a sorted clause list, O((|F|+|M|) w log) literal operations. No kernel, no new variables, no rewriting. Extra clauses never invalidate a certificate; each deleted product clause costs one restriction child. BLQ has neither property.
Lemma SIZE. canon(F + A_i) has at most |F| - |PROD n F| + |A_i| clauses, since a in A_i subsumes every product clause containing it.
Lemma S (sketch, unchecked). If every factor consists of unit clauses, children are restrictions, and refutations pi_i of the children give a resolution refutation of F of size sum|pi_i| + O(|PROD|). So literal-factor UD with variable splits, UP, DP and SCC is polynomially simulated by resolution. For general factors I only have the multiplicative bound |PROD|*sum|pi_i|.

NEON58, ORIGINAL 108 CLAUSES (hand analysis). Clauses 1-36 are exactly PROD of {(-1),(-9)}, {(-3),(-11)}, {(-5),(-13,14),(13,-14)}, {(-7),(-17,18),(17,-18)} (2*2*3*3=36). Clauses 37-72 are the even-side analogue. Each positive group is a two-factor product B_i x C_j, with B_i equivalent to NOT AND(A_i). UD on the left family gives 4 children, and UD on the right family gives 16 leaves. I checked the three leaf types (unit/unit, unit/XOR, XOR/XOR): units shorten the cross clauses and signed SCC meets x==y with x!=y. No variable branch, compression, IALH or dependence on quotient numbering is needed.

RESTRICTED THEOREM (immediate from Lemma UD). If F contains PROD(A_1..A_k), PROD(D_1..D_k') and all B_i x C_j, and each leaf F+A_i+D_j is refuted at cost r, then F is UNSAT after at most 1+k+k*k' step calls. That is about k*k'*(|F|^2 w + r) literal operations with the present quadratic canon, for arbitrary extra clauses. In the k-pair family |F| = 2^(k+1)+k^2, so this is polynomial in encoded bits. It is a statement about this class only.

DISCOVERY (bounded heuristic). From a seed clause, inclusion-minimal symmetric differences between clauses lie inside one factor. Their connected components propose the partition; coarsen and fill M until enumeration passes, under probe's pair budget. Soundness rests only on the check.

FIXTURE (pinned v5, no extension): the k=5 pair family, 20 variables, 89 clauses, pair-adjacent order. Every support block has one forbidden point, so compression skips (all_variables_in_odd_blocks) and the core probe returns no_clauses_removed. Hand trace: variable 1 leaves two states. Variable 11 leaves one, because the pair-zero child is five binary clauses plus 32 width-5 transversals whose first 5-variable window has an empty UP table (transversal width equals IALH k; DP would refute it too). Variables 2 and 12 behave likewise. The survivor is order-isomorphic to the receipted 16-variable fixture under its receipted order. Prediction: UNSAT, peak 2. Non-binding: at k=6 (24 variables, 164 clauses) the empty-table route is gone and DP must replace it.

INDEPENDENT TESTS OF UD. P1: on Neon58's original input both certificates verify by enumerating 36 unions, and all 16 leaves are refuted by canon_plus alone. P2: on the k-pair family, k=4..7, one left split decides every child with zero variable branches. P3: delete one left clause; the formula becomes SAT, the certificate verifies with |M|=1, and the M-child is decided SAT by canon plus pure-literal DP.
missing_theorem:
T-UD-GEN (not proved; this is the exact obstruction). For arbitrary CNF one would need a polynomial p such that every F has a split DAG (variable splits, certified UD splits, canon_plus/DP/IALH leaves) with at most p(B) canonical states, plus polynomial discovery. That would decide SAT in polynomial time. I do not claim it. Once Lemma S is checked, the literal-factor fragment cannot do this for pigeonhole-type families (Haken's resolution bound), so any general result must come from the counting side, not from UD.
Open sub-statements, each independently testable:
(1) Formalise Lemma UD and Lemma S. Then either prove an additive resolution simulation for CNF-factor UD or exhibit a separating family.
(2) Discovery. Maximising absorbed clauses |PROD n F| already contains maximum edge biclique (k=2, width-2 clauses, M empty), which is NP-hard (Peeters 2003, cited from memory). Needed: a class where seed-closure provably finds a certificate within a polynomial factor of optimal.
(3) State bound. Prove sum_layers|states| <= poly(B) under UD for some syntactic class beyond the bipartite product theorem. Nested k-way splits multiply without dedup, and Lemma SIZE alone bounds depth, not width.
(4) A polynomial bit bound for the rank-deficient HNF branch of dual_certificate, or its replacement. Without it even 'work <= poly * states' is unproved for v5.
self_attack:
1. UD adds no proof strength in its literal-factor form (Lemma S). On pigeonhole it only gives balanced at-most-one splits; the measured 8-10 s at h=4 and the h=5 timeout are untouched. Only the elim-before-refute reordering touches that cost, and I have not traced its benefit there.
2. On the Neon58 quotient a pair-adjacent variable order already gives peak 2 (trusted follow-up). UD's gain is order-independence, robustness to extras and smaller IALH inputs. I exhibit no family where every variable order is large and UD is small.
3. Children overlap. A model with several zero pairs is explored once per pair unless canonical residuals coincide. In Neon58 the XOR-factor children may differ syntactically from the unit-factor children, so I claim at most 4 intermediate states, not 1.
4. The restricted theorem assumes the leaf cost r. Leaf refutation by canon_plus alone is hand-checked only for Neon58's three leaf types; general factors may need search inside a block.
5. Discovery is a heuristic. A product hidden behind a renaming of polarities, overlapping factor supports or many deletions (large M) degrades to ordinary branching. P2 for k>=6 rests on a hand simulation of elim's tie-breaking.
6. Fixture risk: four layers are hand-simulated and the rest is inferred from order-isomorphism with an earlier receipt. If IALH derives rows I missed, layer counts change, though I expect peak 2 to survive. Roughly 2000 windows may approach the 20 s candidate limit; a timeout would be inconclusive, not confirmation.
7. Fable73's link-twin text was not supplied to me. The literal-pair case may coincide with it; only CNF factors, the deficit list M and Lemma S would then be new.
mechanism_signature: UD: certified un-distribution. Find an explicit clause family equal, up to a listed deficit M, to a product of clause sets A_1..A_k. Verify by enumerating the product against the input. Branch k+|M| ways into F+A_i and F restricted by not-m. Children are strictly smaller sub-CNFs merged by the existing exact dedup. Nonlinear, kernel-free, no new variables, no rewritten formula, monotone under extra clauses. No more than resolution-strength for literal factors if the unchecked Lemma S holds.
delta_from_prior: BLQ needs a GF(2) kernel and fails on one incompatible block; UD uses no linear structure and tolerates arbitrary extra clauses. Link-twin contraction rewrites literal twins and needs a new checked transformation; UD handles whole CNF factors (Neon58's XOR factors on the raw 108-clause input, before any compression) and its only obligation is an enumeration check. FLS (my previous round) depends on finding a good variable order; UD is order-free and removes the quotient-numbering failure behind peak 8. New here: the deficit list M giving graceful degradation under deleted clauses, Lemma SIZE, the additive resolution simulation sketch that states what UD cannot do, the biclique hardness of optimal discovery, the HNF gap in the work-versus-states bound, and the elim-before-refute reordering.
